summary: Slot-leak suspected after tenant burst run causing gradual p50 throughput ceiling in reserved pool
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 14:05 UTC the customer's dedicated reserved pool (Fluxly Analytics) has exhibited a slow, sustained degradation in median (p50) throughput that flattens at ~60% of baseline during midday windows.
Impact: customer reports increased request latency for batched generation routes and lower overall throughput, causing timeouts in their downstream request broker.
Symptoms are consistent with leaking/retained GPU "slots" after a high-burst tenant workload.
Environment: reserved pool id rp-ff42 (us-east-1), prod.
Observed behavior:
1) p50 throughput drops gradually over ~30-90 minutes after a tenant burst event;
2) GPU attachment counts show stable capacity but effective available slots for batching decrease;
3) autoscaler does not trigger additional attachments because node-level metrics remain below thresholds (no mem pressure), but scheduling logs show repeated short-lived fencing/rewind operations ("alloc-fence" entries) on several GPUs.
Expected behavior: pool should return to baseline throughput within prewarm cooldown and autoscaler should compensate for slot loss or free slots should be reclaimed.
Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-12 14:03 UTC: Fluxly reported a sudden short burst of high-concurrency realtime streams from tenant T-1722 (estimated 1200 concurrent short streams for ~3 minutes).
- 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC: internal alarms (p50 down by 35% vs baseline) triggered.
- 2026-03-12 14:15 UTC: initial triage by support; captured scheduler logs and GPU attach/detach traces.
- 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC: on-call SRE saw persistent batch slot underrun; started deeper tracing.
- 2026-03-13 09:20 UTC: reproduced in control: smaller synthetic burst reproduces similar post-burst p50 ceiling on same pool.
Logs/snippets:
- scheduler: "alloc-fence id=0x7f3 timeout=1200ns node=gpu-42 reason=kv_cache_eviction" (repeated)
- serving-runtime: "batch_slots=48 available_slots=9 reserved_slots=3 leak_hint=slot_refcount_nonzero"
- gpu-manager: "nvlink-reset suppressed; attach_state=FENCED"
Attachments: link to Grafana panels (p50 throughput, available_slots, attach_count): https://grafana.redwood/prod/rp-ff42/dashboards/slot-leak-2026-03-12
Steps to reproduce:
1) On rp-ff42 in prod, issue a 2.5 minute 1100-concurrent short-stream burst across 100ms average stream duration (synthetic harness available in /infra/testharness/burst-run).
2) Observe p50 throughput over next 90 minutes and batch slot accounting.
3) Check scheduler logs for repeated "alloc-fence" messages and serving-runtime leak_hint.
Workarounds attempted by customer:
- Restarting client-side streams (no effect)
- Narrowing request concurrency to 80% of prior peak (temporary improvement)
- No full pool reboot attempted yet by customer
steps_to_reproduce: Run synthetic burst: 1100 concurrent short streams for 150s using infra/testharness/burst-run against rp-ff42
Monitor Grafana: p50 throughput, available_slots, attach_count for 90 minutes post-burst
Tail scheduler logs for 'alloc-fence' and serving-runtime 'leak_hint' entries
comments: 2026-03-12 14:22 - Support (Aisha): Received initial alert from Fluxly; collected sample logs and Grafana links; escalated to SRE.

2026-03-12 15:08 - SRE (Diego): Observed repeated alloc-fence entries on gpu-42/gpu-43 after burst; suspect slot reference leak in prefetcher sidecar (background prefetch thread). Will enable increased debug logs for allocation path.

2026-03-13 09:35 - Support-Escalation (Jamal Weber): Reproduced locally in staging with scaled-down burst; behavior matches production. Opened follow-up PR to add refcount emitters to serving-runtime.

2026-03-14 11:10 - Eng (Priya Nair): Reviewed heap/slot accounting dump; several outstanding slot_refcounts reference a background prefetch task that did not fully decrement on stream termination. Potential root: prefetch cancellation path on brief stream disconnects.
2026-03-14 13:40 - Diego: Running canary build with additional refcount clears in prefetcher on pool rp-ff42 between 14:00-15:00 UTC to validate fix hypothesis.
2026-03-14 15:05 - Customer (Fluxly - Samir): Noted immediate partial improvement during canary window; p50 rose ~18% vs prior plateau. Asked for permanent mitigation timeline.
investigation_notes: Alloc-fence messages appear correlated with ephemeral NV diagnostic suppressions after heavy short-stream bursts.
Serving-runtime emits 'leak_hint' when internal slot_refcount != 0 during expected free; traces point to prefetch sidecar not completing cancellation in edge disconnects.

Autoscaler thresholds conservative: since GPU-level metrics (util, mem) are normal, autoscaler doesn't add capacity; this masks slot-level loss; consider adding slot-availability metric to autoscaler decision path.
Reproduction in staging is consistent; adding refcount emitters provided clearer mapping between streams and slot refs.
resolution_notes: Canary change (serving-runtime PR #2749) deployed with aggressive refcount clear in prefetch cancellation path. Temporary mitigation applied to rp-ff42 during low-risk hours; early results show p50 recovery ~18-22% and gradual reclaim of available_slots. Next steps: 1) push fix to dedicated-pool stable channel after one more 24h canary; 2) update autoscaler to consider slot_availability metric in next sprint; 3) create a runbook to detect slot-leak patterns and automated healing (pool reboot or targeted sidecar restart).
follow_up_actions: Merge PR 2749 to stable and schedule deployment to all affected reserved pools
Add slot_availability metric to autoscaler heuristics (RFC ticket to be created)
Runbook: automated detection and targeted sidecar restart for slot-leak pattern
